name: Working with GGLink
description: How a GGLink project runs, what we need from you and how to reach us.

cards.subject: A project brief
says: is a short written description of what the project must achieve and for whom
gives the agency its starting point before a proposal is written
cards.use: want the agency to understand your goals before it quotes
not: is the final contract that fixes the price

cards.subject: A scope of work
says: lists what will and will not be delivered
is the reference used to decide whether a new request is extra work
cards.use: wonder whether a new request is included in the agreed price
not: is a loose wish list that either side may change at will

cards.subject: A deliverable
says: is a concrete item the agency hands over, such as a finished page template
can be checked against the scope to confirm it is done
cards.use: want to know what you will actually receive at the end of a stage

cards.subject: A sitemap
says: shows the pages of a site and how they are organised
is agreed before design so that no page is forgotten later
cards.use: want to see which pages the site will have and where each one sits
not: is a picture of the final colours and type

cards.subject: A wireframe
says: is a simple layout sketch that shows where content and features sit
lets you comment on structure before colour and imagery are applied
cards.use: want to judge page layout without being distracted by styling
not: shows the final photography and brand colours

cards.subject: A design mock-up
says: shows how a page will look with colours, type and imagery applied
is the first realistic picture of the finished design
cards.use: want to react to the look and feel of a page

cards.subject: Discovery
says: gathers goals, audience and constraints before design starts
reduces the risk of building the wrong thing
cards.use: are at the start of a project and the agency asks many questions about your customers
not: is the final testing stage before launch

cards.subject: A milestone
says: marks a defined point in the timeline, such as design sign-off or launch
lets both sides see whether the project is on track
cards.use: want a checkpoint that shows how far the project has got

cards.subject: A change request
says: records a requirement that falls outside the agreed scope
lets the agency assess the effect on cost and timeline before any work starts
cards.use: want something added that was not in the agreed scope
not: is a complaint that the agency missed a deadline

cards.subject: Scope creep
says: is the gradual growth of a project through small, unrecorded additions
is controlled by treating each addition as a change request
cards.use: notice that small extra asks keep arriving and the launch date keeps drifting
not: happens when the agency delivers less than was agreed

cards.subject: A project assumption
says: is something the plan takes as true, such as content arriving on time
changes cost and timeline when it turns out to be wrong
cards.use: want to know why a plan depends on your content being ready by a date

cards.subject: A dependency
says: is a task that cannot start or finish until something else is done
often sits with the client, such as supplying text or giving approval
cards.use: see that late content is holding up the next stage of work

cards.subject: Success criteria
says: are measurable statements of what a good outcome looks like
let both sides judge the project against more than personal taste
cards.use: want to decide in advance how you will know the project worked

cards.subject: Copy
says: is the written text that appears on the site
is supplied by the client or written by the agency, as agreed in the scope
cards.use: need to know who is responsible for the words on each page

cards.subject: Brand assets
says: include the logo, colours and fonts
keep the site consistent with your other materials
cards.use: are asked what logo and colours the site should use

cards.subject: A content deadline
says: is the date by which text and images are due to the agency
moves the launch date when it is missed
cards.use: want to avoid your content delaying the launch

cards.subject: Placeholder text
says: fills a layout temporarily until real words arrive
must be replaced before the site goes live
cards.use: see Lorem ipsum in a draft design
not: is the final wording approved by the client

cards.subject: Image resolution
says: is the pixel size of a picture
must be large enough for the place the image will be shown
cards.use: find that a photo looks blurry when stretched across a wide banner
not: does not matter on the web

cards.subject: A vector logo
says: scales to any size without blurring
is the best file type to supply for a logo
cards.use: need your logo for both a tiny icon and a large banner
not: is made of a fixed grid of pixels

cards.subject: Stock photography
says: is licensed imagery from a library available to many buyers
can make a site look generic if used without care
cards.use: have no photos of your own team or premises
not: can be used anywhere without checking the licence

cards.subject: An image licence
says: states where and how a picture may be used
is needed for any photo you did not take or commission yourself
cards.use: want to use a photo you found online on your site
not: is only needed for printed material

cards.subject: A testimonial
says: is a customer's statement in praise of your business
should be genuine and used with the permission of the person quoted
cards.use: want to put a customer quote on your site
not: can be invented as long as it sounds plausible

cards.subject: A content audit
says: reviews existing pages to decide what to keep, rewrite or remove
stops out-of-date pages being carried over to a new site
cards.use: are replacing an old site that has years of pages

cards.subject: Permission for supplied material
says: means you must have the right to use the text and images you hand over
protects both client and agency from copyright claims
cards.use: are about to send photos taken by a former colleague or copied from a competitor
not: passes to the agency automatically once material is emailed

cards.subject: Sign-off
says: is your written confirmation that a stage is accepted
lets the agency move on to the next stage
cards.use: are asked to confirm a stage before the work continues

cards.subject: A stakeholder
says: is anyone with an interest in or affected by the project
should be identified early so their needs are heard before design is signed off
cards.use: realise a colleague in another department will use the new site

cards.subject: A designated approver
says: is the one person who gives final answers for your organisation
prevents conflicting instructions from several colleagues
cards.use: want the agency to receive one clear decision rather than many opinions

cards.subject: Design approval
says: confirms the visual direction before pages are built
costs less to change than a page that has already been built
cards.use: are shown the mock-ups and asked to confirm the look

cards.subject: Content approval
says: confirms the final text and images are correct and may go live
is the last chance to correct facts such as prices, names and addresses
cards.use: are asked to check every page for accuracy before publishing

cards.subject: Written approval
says: is an email or signed message recording your decision
provides a record if there is a later disagreement
cards.use: gave a verbal go-ahead on a call and want it recorded
not: is only needed for the final invoice

cards.subject: An approval deadline
says: is the date by which sign-off or comments are due
pushes later milestones back when it is missed
cards.use: want to keep the schedule on track while your team is busy

cards.subject: Final sign-off before launch
says: is the last check that everything is correct to go live
should follow your testing on a staging site
cards.use: are asked whether the site is ready to be published

cards.subject: Approval by committee
says: needs many people to agree before a stage closes
slows projects and tends to produce contradictory feedback
cards.use: find that each colleague's comments undo the last person's

cards.subject: Implied approval
says: is assuming consent because no reply arrived
counts as acceptance only if the agreement says so
cards.use: have gone quiet for two weeks and wonder whether the agency may treat that as a yes
not: is the safest way to confirm a design

cards.subject: A feedback round
says: is one structured pass in which you review work and send comments
is often limited in number by the agreement
cards.use: are asked to review a first draft and reply with changes

cards.subject: Consolidated feedback
says: gathers every reviewer's comments into one list before it is sent
spares the agency from receiving conflicting instructions piecemeal
cards.use: have five colleagues who each want to email the designer
not: is a reply sent separately by each reviewer

cards.subject: Specific feedback
says: names the page, the element and the change wanted
can be acted on faster than a general reaction
cards.use: want to tell the designer exactly what to alter
not: is just saying you do not like it

cards.subject: A draft version number
says: names each draft so that comments refer to the right one
avoids confusion when several versions are in circulation
cards.use: are unsure which of three files your comments apply to

cards.subject: A round limit
says: is the number of revision rounds covered by the agreement
is why extra rounds beyond it are discussed rather than assumed free
cards.use: are on your third round of changes and wonder if more are included
not: means the agency refuses all further changes

cards.subject: Personal preference
says: is a view based on taste rather than on users or goals
is worth weighing against evidence before a change is requested
cards.use: dislike a colour that the whole team otherwise likes

cards.subject: Feedback tied to goals
says: explains the reason for a change in terms of the audience or objective
helps the designer propose a better solution than the literal request
cards.use: want to say why a button needs to be more prominent

cards.subject: Describing the problem
says: tells the designer what is not working and leaves the fix to them
often produces a better answer than a prescribed fix
cards.use: feel the page is hard to scan but cannot say how it should change

cards.subject: Prescribing the fix
says: tells the designer exactly what to do
can rule out a better solution the designer would have found
cards.use: are tempted to dictate font sizes rather than say the text is hard to read

cards.subject: A late-stage change
says: costs more the later it arrives
is best avoided by raising concerns at design sign-off
cards.use: want to move a major section after the pages are built
not: is cheaper than the same change made at wireframe stage

cards.subject: A staging site
says: is a private copy of the site used for testing before it goes live
is not meant to be seen by the public
cards.use: want to test the new site before customers can see it
not: is the live site that visitors use

cards.subject: Go-live
says: is the moment the site becomes visible to the public
often involves pointing the domain at the new site
cards.use: are told the launch is happening tonight

cards.subject: A launch checklist
says: lists the checks done before go-live, such as forms, links and mobile display
gives both sides a shared definition of ready
cards.use: want to see what will be checked before the site goes public

cards.subject: User acceptance testing
says: is you testing the site against what was agreed
is carried out by the client before launch sign-off
cards.use: are asked to try each form and page on the staging site
not: is the agency testing its own code for errors

cards.subject: Cross-browser testing
says: checks the site works in the main web browsers
finds layout faults that appear in only one browser
cards.use: hear that a page looks right in one browser but broken in another

cards.subject: Responsive testing
says: checks the layout on phones, tablets and desktops
catches menus and buttons that are too small to tap
cards.use: want to confirm the site is usable on a phone

cards.subject: A form test
says: confirms an enquiry really reaches the right inbox
includes checking the thank-you page and the notification email
cards.use: want to be sure customers' messages will not disappear

cards.subject: A content freeze
says: is a period when text stops changing so launch stays stable
prevents last-minute edits slipping in untested
cards.use: want to avoid new wording appearing in the days before launch

cards.subject: A 301 redirect
says: sends visitors and search engines from an old address to its new one
protects search ranking when page addresses change
cards.use: are moving to a new site and some page addresses will be different
not: hides a page from search engines for good

cards.subject: A noindex tag
says: asks search engines not to list a page
has to be removed at launch if it was set on the staging site
cards.use: launched but the site is missing from search results
not: makes a page impossible for anyone to open

cards.subject: A rollback plan
says: is the prepared route back to the previous version if launch goes wrong
is decided before launch, not during it
cards.use: worry what happens if the new site fails on the first morning

cards.subject: A domain name
says: is the address people type to reach your site
is registered for a set period and has to be renewed
cards.use: want to know what people type to find you
not: is the place where site files are stored

cards.subject: Hosting
says: is the service that stores the site's files and serves them to visitors
is separate from the registration of the domain name
cards.use: ask where the site actually lives
not: is the address typed into a browser

cards.subject: A domain registrar
says: is the company where a domain is registered
is where renewal reminders and ownership details are held
cards.use: want to know who to contact to renew the domain

cards.subject: HTTPS
says: is the secure version of the web protocol
shows as a padlock in the browser
cards.use: want visitors to see the site as safe

cards.subject: An SSL certificate
says: proves the site is who it says it is
enables encrypted traffic between browser and site
cards.use: are told the certificate has to be installed or renewed

cards.subject: DNS
says: translates a domain name into the address of the server
takes time to update across the internet after a change
cards.use: changed the domain's settings but still see the old site

cards.subject: An A record
says: maps a domain name to a server's IP address
is edited when the website moves to a new server
cards.use: are asked to point the domain at the new server
not: tells the internet which servers handle email

cards.subject: An MX record
says: tells the internet which servers handle email for the domain
can break company email if altered by mistake during a site move
cards.use: worry that moving the site could stop your email

cards.subject: A subdomain
says: is a prefix before the main domain, such as app.example.co.uk
lets a separate service live under the same domain
cards.use: want a separate area such as a client portal under your main address

cards.subject: A TTL
says: says how long a DNS answer may be cached
is lowered ahead of a switch so changes spread faster
cards.use: want the domain switch to take effect quickly

cards.subject: A CDN
says: serves copies of files from locations closer to visitors
speeds up pages for people far from the server
cards.use: have visitors in several countries and want faster pages

cards.subject: Cloudflare
says: sits between visitors and the server to cache and protect
is placed in front of GGLink sites
cards.use: hear that traffic passes through a proxy before reaching the server

cards.subject: Domain ownership
says: should be registered in your organisation's name
lets you keep control of the address if you change agency
cards.use: find the domain is registered to a freelancer's personal account
not: belongs to whoever built the site, by default

cards.subject: Domain expiry
says: lets the address be lost if renewal is missed
is avoided by auto-renew and a current contact email on the account
cards.use: get a renewal reminder at an email address nobody reads

cards.subject: Uptime
says: is the share of time a site is reachable
is a commitment only if a written agreement states it
cards.use: ask how often the site might be unavailable

cards.subject: Website maintenance
says: is the regular work that keeps a site secure, current and working
continues after launch
cards.use: ask what happens to the site once it is live
not: is finished the day the site launches

cards.subject: A backup
says: is a saved copy of site files and data
lets a site be recovered after a mistake or failure
cards.use: want protection against losing the site or its data
not: is the same thing as the live site

cards.subject: A software update
says: installs fixes and security patches for the platform and its add-ons
is delayed at the site's own risk
cards.use: see a notice that the site's platform has a new version

cards.subject: A content update
says: changes text, images or pages on a live site
can often be done by you through the admin area once trained
cards.use: want to change an opening time on a page

cards.subject: A care plan
says: is an ongoing arrangement for updates, backups and fixes after launch
has contents defined by the agreement, not assumed
cards.use: want ongoing support once the project is delivered

cards.subject: Monitoring
says: checks the site automatically and alerts someone when it fails
finds an outage before customers report it
cards.use: want to know the site is down before a customer tells you

cards.subject: A fault
says: is something that does not work as agreed
is raised with the agency as a bug rather than a change request
cards.use: find that a form no longer sends emails although it worked at launch
not: is a new feature you have thought of

cards.subject: An enhancement
says: is a new wish rather than a fault
is estimated and agreed before work starts
cards.use: want a new section added to a live site
not: is fixed free as a defect

cards.subject: End-of-life software
says: no longer receives security fixes
needs an upgrade to be planned before it becomes a risk
cards.use: learn that the site runs on a version its maker has stopped supporting

cards.subject: A restore test
says: proves a backup can really be recovered
finds out that a backup is unusable before an emergency
cards.use: have backups running but have never tried to use one
not: checks the site loads quickly

cards.subject: A strong password
says: is long, unique and not based on personal details
is not reused from another account
cards.use: are creating a login for your site's admin area
not: is a short word with a number at the end

cards.subject: A password manager
says: stores a unique password for every account
lets you share a login without pasting it into an email
cards.use: have too many accounts to remember separate passwords

cards.subject: Two-factor authentication
says: asks for a second proof of identity beyond the password
blocks most takeovers that start with a stolen password
cards.use: want an account to stay safe even if the password leaks
not: replaces the need for a password

cards.subject: Phishing
says: is a fake message that tries to trick you into giving up a login or payment
often imitates a service or colleague you trust
cards.use: get an urgent email asking you to click a link and sign in

cards.subject: Payment-detail fraud
says: is a fake email claiming a supplier's bank details have changed
is defeated by checking the change by phone on a number you already hold
cards.use: receive an invoice that suddenly shows a different bank account
not: is obvious because it always contains spelling errors

cards.subject: Least privilege
says: gives each person only the access their job needs
limits the damage if one account is compromised
cards.use: decide what access a new colleague should have to the site admin
not: gives everyone full administrator access to avoid delays

cards.subject: A shared login
says: is one account used by several people
makes it impossible to tell who made a change
cards.use: want to give two colleagues access by giving them the same password
not: is the recommended way to add team members

cards.subject: Revoking access
says: removes a person's logins when they leave or change role
should include the agency's accounts when a project ends
cards.use: have a staff member leaving who knows the admin password

cards.subject: A CAPTCHA
says: tests whether a form is being submitted by a person
reduces spam enquiries
cards.use: get many junk messages through your contact form

cards.subject: Account lockout
says: blocks sign-in for a while after repeated failed attempts
slows down automated password guessing
cards.use: are locked out after typing the wrong password several times

cards.subject: Personal data
says: is information that identifies a living person, such as a name or email address
comes with legal duties for anyone who collects it
cards.use: want to know whether enquiry form entries count as regulated information
not: covers only financial details

cards.subject: Consent
says: is a person's clear agreement to be contacted or tracked
decides whether you may send marketing email to someone
cards.use: want to email everyone who ever sent you an enquiry
not: can be assumed from a purchase of any kind

cards.subject: A privacy policy
says: explains what personal data a site collects and why
is linked from forms that collect personal details
cards.use: add a contact form that collects names and emails

cards.subject: A cookie banner
says: asks visitors' permission before non-essential cookies are set
has to work properly rather than just display a notice
cards.use: add analytics or advertising tags to the site

cards.subject: A reportable data breach
says: can require notifying the regulator within 72 hours under UK data protection law
includes a downloadable database of customer enquiries
cards.use: discover that a file containing enquiries was publicly downloadable
not: only counts if money was stolen

cards.subject: A support request
says: is a message that asks the agency for help with a problem
is easiest to handle when it goes through the agreed channel
cards.use: find something wrong with the live site

cards.subject: A single support channel
says: keeps requests in one place so none are lost
gives you a record of what was asked and when
cards.use: find that questions are scattered across emails, calls and chat messages

cards.subject: A good bug report
says: states what you did, what you expected and what happened
includes a screenshot or screen recording when possible
cards.use: want to report a page that is not working
not: just says the site is broken

cards.subject: Reproduction steps
says: are the exact actions that make a fault appear
let the agency see the problem for themselves
cards.use: want the agency to find an error that only appears sometimes

cards.subject: Priority
says: reflects how much a problem harms your business
decides which requests are tackled first
cards.use: have a broken checkout and a typo to report on the same day

cards.subject: Response time
says: is how long until someone acknowledges your request
does not promise the problem is fixed
cards.use: ask how quickly you will hear back
not: is the time until the fault is fixed

cards.subject: Resolution time
says: is how long until the problem is fixed
depends on how complex the fault is
cards.use: ask how soon the fix will be live
not: is the time until someone acknowledges the request

cards.subject: A service level
says: states the response and fix targets a provider commits to
is only relied on if it is written down
cards.use: are told support is fast but no figures are given

cards.subject: Escalation
says: is the route to a more senior person when a request is stuck
is used after the normal channel has failed to resolve it
cards.use: have waited well past the stated response time with no reply

cards.subject: Handover documentation
says: records how the site is built and where its accounts live
lets someone else support the site if the agency changes
cards.use: want to be able to move to another provider without losing knowledge

cards.subject: A training session
says: shows your team how to edit the site themselves
reduces the number of small requests sent to the agency
cards.use: want your team to update pages without the agency

cards.subject: Responsive design
says: adapts the layout to the width of the screen
avoids a separate site for phones
cards.use: want one site that works on phones and desktops

cards.subject: SEO
says: improves how well a site can be found in search results
combines relevant content, clear structure and sound technical set-up
cards.use: want more people to find the site through search
not: guarantees first place in search results

cards.subject: A call to action
says: is a button or link that asks the visitor to take a step
gives each page a clear next move
cards.use: want visitors to book, buy or call from a page

cards.subject: A meta title
says: is the page title shown in search results and browser tabs
should be unique to each page
cards.use: want to control the headline shown in search results

cards.subject: A meta description
says: is the summary text shown under a title in search results
can influence whether people click through
cards.use: want to control the snippet shown under the result

cards.subject: Analytics
says: measures how visitors find and use the site
shows which pages and actions matter
cards.use: want to know which pages people actually visit

cards.subject: Alt text
says: describes an image in words for screen readers
displays if the image fails to load
cards.use: are asked to supply descriptions for your site's photos

cards.subject: Accessibility
says: lets people with disabilities use the site
is also good for users in difficult conditions such as bright sunlight
cards.use: want people using screen readers to be able to use your site

cards.subject: Colour contrast
says: is the difference in brightness between text and background
affects whether text can be read by people with low vision
cards.use: find that pale grey text on white is hard to read

cards.subject: WCAG
says: is the set of international guidelines for accessible web content
is cited when judging whether a site meets an accessibility standard
cards.use: want to know what standard an accessible site is measured against

cards.subject: Page speed
says: is how quickly a page loads and becomes usable
is hurt by oversized images
cards.use: hear that visitors leave when pages are slow

cards.subject: A conversion
says: is a visitor completing a wanted action, such as sending an enquiry
is the measure of whether a page does its job
cards.use: want to count how many visitors become enquiries
not: is any visit to the home page

cards.subject: An XML sitemap
says: lists a site's pages for search engines
helps search engines discover new pages
cards.use: want search engines to find all your pages
not: is the planning diagram of pages for the design stage

cards.subject: A robots file
says: tells well-behaved crawlers which areas not to fetch
does not protect private content from being opened
cards.use: want to keep an admin area out of search results
not: is a secure way to hide confidential pages

cards.subject: A quote
says: states the price for a defined piece of work
is only as firm as the scope it describes
cards.use: want to know what the work will cost
not: is a promise that any later request is free

cards.subject: A fixed price
says: sets the cost for a defined scope
changes only when the scope changes
cards.use: want certainty about the cost for an agreed list of work

cards.subject: Time and materials
says: bills for the time actually spent
suits work whose scope cannot be fully known in advance
cards.use: are exploring an idea and cannot list every requirement yet

cards.subject: A payment schedule
says: states when each payment falls due
is often tied to milestones
cards.use: want to know when invoices will arrive

cards.subject: A project manager
says: coordinates the schedule, people and approvals
is the person to ask about progress and dates
cards.use: want to know who to ask about the status of the project

cards.subject: Recurring costs
says: continue after launch, such as hosting, domain renewals and licences
should be listed so there are no surprises
cards.use: budget only for the build and want to know what comes after
not: end on the day of launch

cards.subject: A third-party licence
says: covers paid plugins, fonts or themes the site uses
may renew yearly and need budgeting
cards.use: are told the site uses a paid add-on

cards.subject: Ownership of the finished work
says: is stated in the agreement, including when it passes to you
should be understood before the project begins
cards.use: want to know who owns the design and code once the project ends
not: is always the client's from the first day of work

cards.subject: Acceptance criteria
says: define what must work for a deliverable to count as accepted
are agreed before the work is built
cards.use: want to agree what done means for a contact form

cards.subject: The GGLink contact form
says: sends the GGLink team a notification email for each enquiry
lands the visitor on a thank-you page after sending
cards.use: want to know what happens when you send GGLink an enquiry

cards.subject: The GGLink enquiry spam check
says: uses Google reCAPTCHA to filter spam submissions
helps keep genuine enquiries from being buried
cards.use: wonder how GGLink keeps junk out of its contact form

cards.subject: A GGLink app address
says: follows the pattern app name then .gglink.co.uk
gives each GGLink app its own subdomain
cards.use: want to know where to find a GGLink app such as GGSocial or GGLearn

cards.subject: A GGLink release backup
says: is taken before each release of a site
means there is a copy to recover from if data is damaged
cards.use: want reassurance about what GGLink does before changing a live site

cards.subject: A GGLink rollback
says: restores the previous files after a bad release
leaves live data such as enquiries untouched
cards.use: ask what happens to enquiries that arrive between a release and a rollback
not: restores the whole database to the state before the release

cards.subject: The GGLink HTTPS redirect
says: sends visitors from plain HTTP to the secure version
sends the non-www address to the www address
cards.use: type the address without www or https and want to know where you land

cards.subject: GGLink certificate renewal
says: happens automatically for GGLink app certificates
does not need you to do anything
cards.use: ask who renews the security certificate on a GGLink app
not: is a manual job the client does each year

cards.subject: The GGLink admin sign-in
says: limits repeated failed attempts with a temporary lockout
uses roles so owners and editors have different powers
cards.use: want to know how access to the GGLink admin area is protected

cards.subject: GGLink email consent
says: is recorded for every contact so that bulk email goes only to people who agreed
excludes people who unsubscribed
cards.use: want to know who GGLink may send marketing email to

cards.subject: GGLink prices and results
says: are only published when they are real and can be evidenced
should be confirmed with GGLink in writing before you rely on them
cards.use: see a price or a result quoted and want to know how far to rely on it
not: can be assumed from a competitor's website

cards.subject: GGLink email delivery
says: is set up by verifying the whole domain with the email service
helps notifications avoid the spam folder
cards.use: are not seeing enquiry notifications in your inbox

qa.q: What is a project brief?
qa.right: A short written description of what the project must achieve and for whom
wrong: A legal contract that fixes the final price
A list of the pages that will be built
A report on how the finished site performed
qa.why: The brief gives the agency its starting point before it proposes anything.

qa.q: Which of these is hosting?
qa.right: The service that stores the site's files and serves them to visitors
wrong: The address people type to reach the site
The padlock shown beside the address
qa.why: The domain is the address; hosting is where the files live.

qa.q: Why does an agency ask for your logo, colours and fonts?
qa.right: So the site stays consistent with your other materials
wrong: So it can sell them to other clients
Because the law requires a logo on every site
So it can skip the design stage
qa.why: Brand assets keep the site recognisably yours.

qa.q: What does sign-off mean on a project?
qa.right: You confirm in writing that a stage is accepted
wrong: The agency confirms it has started work
The final invoice has been paid
qa.why: Sign-off lets the agency move on to the next stage.

qa.q: What is a staging site used for?
qa.right: Testing the site privately before it goes live
wrong: Serving the public site to visitors
qa.why: Staging is a private rehearsal copy.

qa.q: What does the padlock in a browser's address bar tell a visitor?
qa.right: The connection between their browser and the site is encrypted
wrong: The site's content has been checked for accuracy
The company behind the site is trustworthy
qa.why: The padlock reflects encrypted traffic, not the honesty or total safety of the site.

qa.q: What is a new request judged against when deciding whether it is included in the agreed price?
qa.right: The agreed scope of work
wrong: The size of the request alone
qa.why: The scope of work is the reference for what is included.

qa.q: A client emails three small extra requests each week and the launch keeps slipping. What is happening?
qa.right: Scope creep
qa.why: Small unrecorded additions growing a project are scope creep.

qa.q: Why should feedback from five colleagues be gathered into one list before it goes to the designer?
qa.right: So the agency does not receive conflicting instructions piecemeal
wrong: Because designers only read one email a week
So it counts as a single round of the agreement
Because feedback should never mention names
qa.why: One consolidated list avoids contradiction and wasted effort.

qa.q: A first draft is shown with grey boxes and no photography. What is it?
qa.right: A wireframe
qa.why: Wireframes show structure without styling.

qa.q: Which feedback is easiest for a designer to act on?
qa.right: The heading on the services page is too small to read on a phone
qa.why: Specific feedback names the element and the problem.

qa.q: The agency asks who gives final answers for your organisation. Why?
qa.right: One decision-maker prevents conflicting instructions
wrong: Because only one person can legally sign
To reduce the number of invoices
Because they must be the most senior person
qa.why: A designated approver keeps decisions clear.

qa.q: What does the domain registrar do?
qa.right: Holds the registration of your domain name
wrong: Stores the pages of your site
Writes the text for your pages
qa.why: The registrar is where the domain is registered and renewed.

qa.q: Which statement about recurring costs is correct?
qa.right: Hosting, domain renewals and licences continue after launch
wrong: They apply only to large organisations
They are paid to the registrar once for life
qa.why: Budget for what continues after the build.

qa.q: Why must placeholder text be replaced before launch?
qa.right: It is only there to fill the layout until real words arrive
wrong: Search engines refuse to index it
It is licensed only for the design stage
qa.why: Leaving Lorem ipsum live looks unfinished.

qa.q: What does a care plan usually provide?
qa.right: Ongoing updates, backups and fixes, as defined in the agreement
qa.why: What a care plan includes is set by the agreement, not assumed.

qa.q: You change your domain's DNS settings and still see the old site. What is the most likely reason?
qa.right: DNS changes take time to spread across the internet
wrong: The registrar has locked the domain
The browser is blocking the page
qa.why: Cached DNS answers expire over time.

qa.q: A colleague suggests using a stock photo they found by searching online. What should you check first?
qa.right: That you have a licence that allows its use on your site
wrong: That it is a large enough file for print
That it has no people in it
That the file name is short
qa.why: A photo you did not take or buy needs an image licence.

qa.q: After you gave a verbal go-ahead on a call, the agency asks you to confirm by email. Why?
qa.right: A written approval gives both sides a record
wrong: So the agency can charge for the call
qa.why: Written approval avoids later disagreement.

qa.q: A client has been quiet for two weeks and the agency continues, treating that as approval. Under what condition is that acceptable?
qa.right: Only if the agreement says silence counts as acceptance
wrong: Only if the agency is senior
qa.why: Implied approval depends on the agreement.

qa.q: Your contact form worked at launch but no longer sends emails. What kind of request is this?
qa.right: A fault, because the form does not work as agreed
qa.why: Something that does not work as agreed is a fault.

qa.q: You want a new booking section on a live site. How is it normally handled?
qa.right: It is estimated and agreed before work starts
wrong: It is added free as a defect
It is held until the next care plan renewal
qa.why: A new wish is an enhancement or change request.

qa.q: Which best describes the difference between response time and resolution time?
qa.right: Response time is acknowledgement; resolution time is the fix
wrong: Response time is the fix; resolution time is the acknowledgement
Response time is billed; resolution time is free
qa.why: Acknowledging a request does not mean it is solved.

qa.q: Why is an A record changed during a site move?
qa.right: It points the domain to the new server
wrong: It sets who may receive email
It lists pages for search engines
qa.why: The A record maps a name to an IP address.

qa.q: Where is it safest to share a login with a colleague?
qa.right: Through a password manager's sharing feature
wrong: In the subject line of an email
In a text message together with the username
On a sticky note on the monitor
qa.why: A password manager shares access without exposing the password in transit.

qa.q: What is the best reason to have your domain registered in your organisation's name?
qa.right: You keep control of the address if you change agency
wrong: It makes the site load faster
It removes the need for hosting
qa.why: The registrant controls the domain.

qa.q: A staff member who knew the admin password has left. What should you do?
qa.right: Remove their access and change shared credentials
wrong: Wait to see if anything goes wrong
Tell nobody so that attackers are not alerted
qa.why: Revoke access when people leave.

qa.q: Which action keeps a website secure after launch?
qa.right: Applying software updates and security patches regularly
wrong: Turning off backups to save space
qa.why: Maintenance is ongoing.

qa.q: What is the main purpose of a content freeze before launch?
qa.right: To stop last-minute edits slipping in untested
wrong: To stop visitors using the site
To prevent the domain from expiring
To lock the agency out of the server
qa.why: Stable content makes launch testing meaningful.

qa.q: Why test every form on the staging site before launch?
qa.right: To confirm enquiries really reach the right inbox
wrong: To see how many visitors arrive
qa.why: A form that does not deliver loses customers silently.

qa.q: Why might a page look right in one browser but broken in another?
qa.right: Browsers can interpret the code differently
wrong: The site is hosted on two servers
The CDN has been turned off
qa.why: Cross-browser testing catches these cases.

qa.q: A supplier's email says their bank details have changed and asks you to pay the next invoice to a new account. What should you do first?
qa.right: Check the change by phone using a number you already hold
wrong: Pay it to avoid late fees
Reply asking them to confirm in the same email thread
Forward the email to colleagues for a vote
qa.why: Payment-detail fraud depends on you trusting the email alone.

qa.q: The new site is missing from search results, and the staging site had been hidden from search. What should be checked first?
qa.right: Whether a noindex setting was left in place
wrong: Whether the domain is too short
Whether the logo is a vector file
qa.why: A noindex tag set on staging can survive into the live site.

qa.q: You are moving to a new site whose page addresses differ from the old ones. What protects your search ranking?
qa.right: 301 redirects from old addresses to new ones
wrong: A noindex tag on all new pages
qa.why: Redirects tell search engines where pages moved.

qa.q: Visitors in another country find pages slow to load. What could help?
qa.right: A CDN that serves files from closer locations
qa.why: CDNs shorten the distance to visitors.

qa.q: A designer receives the comment 'make the text 18px and bold'. A better comment would be:
qa.right: The text is hard to read on a phone; can it be easier to scan?
wrong: Use the same font as our competitor
qa.why: Describing the problem allows the designer to find the best fix.

qa.q: Your team keeps contradicting each other in feedback on a design. What is the best fix?
qa.right: Appoint one approver and send consolidated feedback
wrong: Ask the agency to choose for you
Wait for the committee to agree on everything
qa.why: Approval by committee slows the project.

qa.q: You discover that a database file containing customer enquiries could be downloaded by anyone. How should you treat it?
qa.right: As a possible data breach that may need reporting
qa.why: Exposed personal data can trigger reporting duties.

qa.q: After a bad release the agency restores the previous site files but not the database. Why?
qa.right: So enquiries that arrived since the release are not lost
wrong: Because databases are backed up weekly only
qa.why: Code can be rolled back without discarding new data.

qa.q: You pay for a plugin that the site uses. When it renews, who should expect to pay?
qa.right: Whoever the agreement says is responsible for third-party licences
qa.why: Third-party licences should be listed in the agreement.

qa.q: A site runs on a version of its software that is no longer supported. What is the right response?
qa.right: Plan an upgrade before it becomes a security risk
wrong: Ignore it as long as the site loads
qa.why: End-of-life software does not receive fixes.

qa.q: Why should backups be tested by restoring them?
qa.right: A backup that has never been restored might not work
wrong: It is required by the registrar
qa.why: A restore test proves the backup is usable.

qa.q: Which is a sensible way to stop a launch day going wrong?
qa.right: Prepare a rollback plan beforehand
wrong: Hide the domain from the agency
qa.why: Decide how to go back before you go forward.

qa.q: The agency promises very fast support but gives no figures. What should you do?
qa.right: Ask for response and fix targets in writing
qa.why: A service level only counts if it is written down.

qa.q: A request has waited past the stated response time with no reply from the normal channel. What next?
qa.right: Escalate to a senior contact using the agreed route
qa.why: Escalation is the route for stuck requests.

qa.q: A client wants every colleague to approve each page. What is the likely consequence?
qa.right: Slower sign-off and contradictory feedback
qa.why: Approval by committee adds delay.

qa.q: You want to use customer quotes that were collected years ago. What should you do?
qa.right: Confirm the people agree to be quoted and that the quotes are genuine
qa.why: Testimonials need to be genuine and used with permission.

qa.q: A page still receives search traffic but its content is out of date. What does a content audit help decide?
qa.right: What to keep, rewrite or remove
qa.why: An audit assesses each page.

qa.q: You are comparing quotes and one is much cheaper because it excludes several items. What is the best response?
qa.right: Compare the scopes before comparing the prices
qa.why: A price is only meaningful against its scope.

qa.q: A colleague insists an old pricing page looks wrong. The agency finds the page is correct. What does this show?
qa.right: Feedback should be tied to goals and evidence, not hunches
qa.why: Personal preference should be checked before requesting changes.

qa.q: Why lower the TTL on a DNS record ahead of a switch?
qa.right: Changes spread faster once the record is updated
wrong: It makes the site load faster
It removes the need for hosting
qa.why: A short TTL means caches expire sooner.

qa.q: A price you saw on a competitor's website is described as typical. Should you rely on it when planning your own budget?
qa.right: No, rely only on a written quote for your own scope
wrong: No, because prices are never public
qa.why: Quotes depend on scope.
